title: Theo and the Border
premise: Ivo Blackwood, a financial-crimes investigator whose work is deliberately kept anonymous, discovers that the safe house protecting their current case has been listed for sale online — with interior photos exposing its location and its occupants. The listing traces back to a laundering network Ivo once helped dismantle, now rebuilt under new ownership and planning an attack on a border crossing designed to look like an industrial accident. As Ivo races to expose the plot, they must decide whether to protect the colleagues who buried evidence to shield them or burn the whole network down with the truth. In the end, Ivo chooses truth over loyalty, testifying publicly at devastating personal cost, and the attack is stopped hours before detonation — but the person who leaked the safe house was someone Ivo trusted most.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write from a small coastal town and refuse interviews about which cases inspired their thrillers.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We meet Ivo mid-investigation, uncredited by design, drowning in paperwork for a case no one wants named. The emotional beat is quiet resentment: competence without recognition, and the first hint that someone inside the agency resents it too.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A colleague sends a real-estate link: the safe house, photographed room by room, listed as a 'renovation opportunity.' Ivo recognizes the bookshelf, the kettle, the witness sleeping upstairs. Panic sets in; the beat is cold dread arriving through something as mundane as a property portal.

chapters.title: Room 4
chapters.summary: Witness Mara Voss's POV. Inside the safe house, Mara senses the handlers' sudden tension but not its cause. She catalogs small details — a changed guard rotation, a silenced phone — trusting her instincts over their reassurances. The beat is claustrophobic innocence about to end.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A chaotic night move of Mara to a second location. Ivo notices the extraction route was known in advance — someone fed it to the movers. Suspicion turns inward. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing the enemy may wear your badge.

chapters.title: Shell Game
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tracing the listing's seller, Ivo finds a shell company with fingerprints matching the Halvard network — the laundering ring Ivo helped dismantle three years ago, officially dead. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried, and pride curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Corridor broker Elias Renner reviews the operation: an 'accident' at the Kestrel border crossing, timed to destroy records held in a customs depot. He admires Ivo's persistence from a distance. Beat: elegant, patient menace; power that never needs to raise its voice.

chapters.title: Old Loyalties
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confronts Deputy Director Sorrel, who admits the original Halvard case was closed early to protect a political ally. Sorrel asks Ivo to let it go — again. Beat: the seductive weight of institutional loyalty versus the itch of truth.

chapters.title: What Mara Saw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reveals she wasn't a random witness: she processed payments for Halvard's front companies and kept a private ledger out of self-protection. She offers it — if Ivo gets her out of the country. Beat: wary alliance, two people using each other honestly.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The ledger names a current official — initials matching Sorrel's deputy, Callum Reeve. But the entries could be forged. Ivo can't tell if Mara is a witness or a weapon pointed at the agency. Beat: doubt poisoning every certainty.

chapters.title: Kestrel Crossing
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs. A mosaic chapter: a customs clerk, a truck driver, a depot guard — ordinary lives stacked around the target site. The reader sees what none of them can. Beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo's access is revoked overnight; the investigation is reassigned to Reeve. Officially, Ivo is a liability. Unofficially, Ivo is being walled off from the very attack they're trying to stop. Beat: betrayal wearing procedure's face.

chapters.title: The Second Safe House
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The replacement safe house is compromised too — same listing trick, different agent. Mara realizes the leak isn't a file; it's a person with full operational knowledge. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve; she stops waiting to be saved.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer
chapters.summary: Renner POV shifting to a tense meeting. Renner approaches Ivo indirectly through an intermediary: walk away, and Mara lives and the crossing stays intact. He frames it as mercy. Beat: temptation with a human face — power corrupting by offering kindness.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Confession
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Sorrel admits the original cover-up, and worse: the safe house listings are Reeve's insurance policy, leverage against everyone who knew. Sorrel begs Ivo to go public quietly, after the fact. Beat: a loyal man choosing loyalty one last time, at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cross-referencing shipping manifests and the ledger, Ivo pins the attack window: four days, Kestrel depot, disguised as a hazmat incident. But going official means revealing Mara's illegal ledger. Beat: the cost of truth calculated in real time.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Ivo and Mara's alternating POV. Off the books, the two build the case themselves — old contacts, burner phones, a journalist who owes Ivo nothing and agrees anyway. Beat: improbable hope; the pleasure of competence reunited with purpose.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The leak pattern finally resolves: it's not Reeve. It's Dana, Ivo's closest colleague, feeding locations to Renner to pay off debts Halvard's successors hold over her family. Beat: heartbreak — loyalty corrupted not by ambition but love.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Reeve moves to destroy the ledger; Renner accelerates the timeline; Dana, cornered by Ivo, gives up the detonation method in exchange for her brother's safety. Beat: every thread pulled taut, all lies colliding at once.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Climax, Ivo's POV. At the crossing, Ivo triggers the depot's emergency protocols minutes before the staged blast, forcing the 'accident' into daylight while Mara's ledger goes live via the journalist. Renner is taken quietly; Reeve runs. Beat: adrenaline resolving into hard-won clarity.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Public hearing: Ivo names names, including Sorrel's early cover-up and their own years of comfortable complicity. Career destroyed, name finally spoken aloud. Beat: catharsis with a bill attached — truth costs exactly what it's worth.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Free, under a new name, Mara reads about the hearings from afar and mails her original ledger pages to no one — keeping the last copy for herself. Beat: survival without absolution; memory as both burden and armor.

chapters.title: Theo and the Border
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ivo visits the abandoned safe house, now genuinely for sale, and meets Theo — a young investigator assigned to review the fallout — at the border where it nearly happened. Ivo passes on what they learned: borders don't keep corruption out; only witnesses do. Beat: quiet, earned hope, and the torch handed on.
